samples.summary: toggleQuote cannot un-quote a blockquote that contains blank lines
samples.evidence: `const quoted = lines.every((l) => QUOTE_RE.test(l.text));` — QUOTE_RE is /^\s*>\s?/ , which never matches an empty line. Selecting a normal multi-paragraph quote (`> a`, ``, `> b`) therefore evaluates `quoted === false`, so pressing Quote adds a second level of markers (`> > a`, `> `, `> > b`) instead of unquoting. There is no way to un-quote such a block from the toolbar; repeated presses only nest deeper.

samples.summary: toggleQuote includes an extra line when the selection ends at a line start
samples.evidence: `const last = state.doc.lineAt(to).number;` — for the common editor gesture of selecting whole lines (e.g. from 0 to 4 in "one\ntwo", where `to` is exactly the start of line 2), `lineAt(to)` returns line 2, so the following, visually unselected line is also quoted/unquoted. The usual convention is to exclude that line when `to === lineAt(to).from && to > from`.

samples.summary: Un-quoting strips the line's leading indentation along with the marker
samples.evidence: `const marker = QUOTE_RE.exec(l.text)![0];` with QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/ — for a line like `"    > text"` the match is `"    > "`, so the deletion `{from: l.from, to: l.from + marker.length}` removes the four-space indentation too. Quote→unquote is therefore not round-trip safe: indented quoted content (e.g. inside a list item) is silently de-indented, which can change how the surrounding markdown parses.

samples.summary: insertFoldout inserts into the middle of a non-empty selection instead of replacing/leaving it
samples.evidence: `const pos = state.selection.main.head;` plus `changes: { from: pos, insert }` (no `to`). With a non-empty selection the skeleton is injected at the *head*; for a backward selection (head < anchor, e.g. shift+Left) that head sits at the start of the selected region, so the skeleton is spliced into the middle of the selected text, splitting a word or a paragraph. Nothing is deleted, but the result is a mangled document rather than either wrapping or replacing the selection.

samples.summary: insertCodeBlock produces a stray blank line (and can break the fence) for line-wise selections / selections that contain a fence
New API methods can mutate a read-only note (read-only enforced only in the toolbar)
samples.evidence: `toggleQuote: () => toggleQuote(view)`, `insertCodeBlock`, `insertFoldout` dispatch changes directly. editor.ts:355 configures only `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)`, which blocks user input but not programmatic `view.dispatch`, and no `EditorState.readOnly` facet is set. The only gate is notes-toolbar.tsx:237 (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`) hiding the buttons, so any other caller of the exported NoteEditorAPI (e.g. notes-detail.tsx/notes-view.tsx passing the API out) can edit a read-only note. Pre-existing shape for toggleBold, but the new methods widen the surface.

samples.summary: Flush-left foldout insert silently terminates an enclosing list/blockquote
samples.evidence: `const prefix = pos === line.from ? '' : '\n';` writes `<details>` at column 0 regardless of context. details-plugin.ts:104 registers the rule with `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote','list']`, i.e. as a terminator, so inserting a foldout while the caret is inside a list item or blockquote ends that list/quote and the remainder of the item is re-parsed at top level — the surrounding structure changes as a side effect of the insert. The doc comment justifies flush-left only against indented-code parsing, not this case.
